title: Quantum Block Turbo Codes
authors: Khaled Jebari, Luiz Anet Neto, Ramesh Pyndiah, Jean-Louis de Bougrenet de la Tocnaye
abstract: In the early nineties, the introduction of turbo codes revolutionized classical error correction. The idea was mainly applied on two types of codes: convolutional turbo codes and turbo product codes. The first type of codes was adapted to quantum error correction which initiated the theory of quantum serial turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for quantum block turbo codes, the quantum analog of the second type of turbo codes. We describe their iterative decoding algorithm and simulate their performances on a depolarizing channel for different constituent codes.
summary: This paper introduces Quantum Block Turbo Codes (QBTC) as a powerful framework for quantum error correction, extending classical turbo coding concepts to the quantum domain. It details an iterative decoding algorithm that exchanges soft information between constituent code decoders. The work demonstrates that QBTCs achieve superior error correction rates, exhibiting a measurable 'turbo decoding effect' for multiple logical qubits.
main_problem: The paper develops a theory and decoding algorithm for Quantum Block Turbo Codes (QBTC), aiming to improve quantum error correction performance by creating a quantum analog of classical product codes.
main_result: QBTCs allow for flexible encoding and decoding using iterative soft-information exchange between inner and outer decoders, demonstrating a clear 'turbo decoding effect' when using larger constituent codes.
method: The core method involves an iterative maximum likelihood decoding technique that exchanges soft information between row and column decoding blocks, analogous to classical turbo decoding.
model_or_system: The system uses Quantum Error Correction Codes (QECCs), specifically stabilizer codes, which are combined in a product structure using two constituent codes, $C_1$ and $C_2$. The encoding is implemented via a unitary transformation $V$ acting on physical qubits.
key_observables: Logical error rates, syndrome measurements ($S$), and the performance comparison against minimum weight (MW) decoders.
important_parameters: Code parameters $(n_1, k_1)$ and $(n_2, k_2)$, and the depolarizing channel noise rate.
main_assumptions: The decoding process must operate at the level of logical operators due to inherent degeneracy in stabilizer codes, and the M & R procedure requires careful probabilistic handling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the encoding matrix structure, the global view of the 2D product code encoding/decoding, and detailed diagrams of the SISO inner and outer decoding blocks.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the quantum analogy to classical turbo codes, detailing the encoding/decoding using two constituent codes, formalizing the soft-information exchange via M & R procedures, and finally extending the theory to multi-layer product codes.
why_interesting: It provides a structured, iterative decoding framework for quantum codes that mimics successful classical techniques, offering a pathway to better performance in fault-tolerant quantum computation.
